To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Gricean Maxims are a useful guide for selecting information to communicate to human users, (b) modified versions of standard algorithms can be used to implement the Gricean Maxim, (c) the modified algorithms can be used in a pipeline to select the most important information to communicate from a large amount of data, and (d) the resulting information is useful to human users.

(i) Gricean maxima are a key element in adapting data analysis algorithms so that they can be used for effective communication of data to human users; (ii) the Gricean maxim of Quality is particularly useful in data analysis, as it can help us to identify the most important patterns and trends in data; and (iii) Gricean maxim-based data analysis can lead to better data summaries than traditional data analysis, as shown in a user experiment.

(a) we can use modified versions of standard algorithms for data analysis to select important information to communicate, (b) these modifications are motivated by the Gricean Maxims, and (c) these algorithms can be used to generate English textual summaries.
